newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga restarts Snorre, to close Tordis.
newsitem.headline: Saga restarts Snorre, to close Tordis.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Friday it had restarted oil output at the 230,000 barrel per day (bpd) Snorre oilfield in the North Sea after a tanker began loading crude at the Statfjord development.
But, it said, it planned to shut in output at the 82,000 bpd Tordis field due to burgeoning storage capacity at the Gullfaks C platform.
Snorre pumps crude to Statfjord A for final processing, storage and loading on to shuttle tankers, meanwhile Tordis is tied-back to the Gullfaks C installation.
North Sea loadings by shuttle tankers have been severely disrupted recently due to hurricane-force winds and high swell.

"They have started loadings at Statfjord and we resumed production at Snorre at around 1230 GMT," Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag told Reuters. "We will go back to normal production as soon as possible."
Schibevaag said Tordis would close down at 1530 GMT if vessels were unable to begin loadings at Gullfaks before that time.
The 30,000 bpd Vigdis field, which pumps oil to Snorre for processing before being piped to Gullfaks A for shipping, was shut down late on Thursday with gas compressor problems.
Schibevaag said Vigdis would remain closed until Saturday or Sunday.
